answer:
**Lady Godiva's husband, Leofric, was Earl of Mercia.**

Mercia was an **Anglo-Saxon kingdom** (not specifically "Anglic") that existed in early medieval England. It was one of the Seven Kingdoms (Heptarchy) of Anglo-Saxon England and was centred on the River Trent and its tributaries. 

During Lady Godiva's lifetime in the 11th century (died c. 1067), Mercia was still considered an important earldom within England. Leofric became Earl of Mercia around the early 11th century, becoming one of the most powerful noblemen in England under King Edward the Confessor and King Cnut the Great. Both he and Lady Godiva were well-known for their patronage of the church, particularly founding and endowing monasteries at Coventry and Much Wenlock.
